questions.question: Define biodiversity loss. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Define biodiversity loss.
  • ● Reduction in variety of plants, animals, and microorganisms
  • ● Includes loss of species, genes, and ecosystems
  • ● Caused by deforestation, pollution, climate change, overexploitation
  • ● Leads to ecological imbalance
  • ● Threatens food chain and human survival
  • ● Results in extinction of species

questions.question: Describe the structure of the tundra ecosystem. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the structure of the tundra ecosystem.
  • ● Treeless cold biome found in polar regions
  • ● Extremely low temperature and short growing season
  • ● Soil remains frozen (permafrost)
  • ● Vegetation includes mosses, lichens, grasses, small shrubs
  • ● Animals include polar bears, reindeer, Arctic foxes
  • ● Low biodiversity and low productivity
  • ● Simple food chain due to harsh climate

questions.question: Differentiate between biotic and abiotic components with examples. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between biotic and abiotic components with examples.
  • Biotic Components
  • ● Living components of ecosystem
  • ● Includes plants, animals, microorganisms
  • ● Show growth and reproduction
  • ● Examples: trees, humans, bacteria
  • Abiotic Components
  • ● Non-living physical factors
  • ● Includes air, water, sunlight, soil, temperature
  • ● Influence survival of organisms
  • ● Examples: rainfall, minerals, humidity

  • ● Construction dust and road dust
  • ● Firecrackers during festivals
  • ● Winter temperature inversion trapping pollutants
  • ● High population and urbanization
  • ● Weak implementation of pollution control measures

  • ● Poor people depend heavily on natural resources
  • ● Poverty leads to overuse of forests and land
  • ● Lack of awareness increases pollution and waste
  • ● Environmental degradation reduces agricultural productivity
  • ● Natural disasters affect poor communities more
  • ● Poor sanitation and waste management harm environment
  • ● Creates a vicious cycle between poverty and degradation
